Complete band(score): return "high" for scores at least 80, "middle" for scores at least 50 but below 80, and "low" otherwise. Inputs are numbers.
Complete choose_name(name): return name when it is nonempty text, otherwise return "Explorer". Do not convert the result to a Boolean.
Complete compare_lists(left, right): return a tuple containing value equality first and object identity second. Do not copy or change either list.
Complete above_limit(scores, limit): build a new dictionary retaining only entries whose score is greater than limit. Preserve keys and scores, and leave scores unchanged.
Complete order_by_last(values): return a new sorted list of nonempty strings, ordered by each string's last character. Use a key function; preserve the input list. Equal keys retain input order.
Complete has_negative(values): return True if at least one number is below zero, otherwise False. Use a for loop with break and loop else; an empty list has no negative values.
Complete repeat_text(text, /, count=2): return text repeated count times. text must remain positional-only; count may be passed by position or keyword. Inputs are text and a nonnegative integer.

Implement route(command) with match/case. ["greet", name] returns "Hello " plus name only when name is a string; ["pause"] returns "Paused"; everything else returns "Unknown". Accept matching tuples too and preserve input.
Write utf8_summary(text). Encode the supplied valid Unicode string as UTF-8 and return (byte_count, decoded_text). Preserve exact text without normalization; empty text returns (0, "").
Implement close_readings(a, b) for finite real-number inputs using math.isclose with rel_tol=1e-6 and abs_tol=1e-9. Return the Boolean result, without rounding or modifying inputs.

Use supplied greeting_tool.py. Import it without calling its demonstration and implement personal_greeting(name) by returning greeting_tool.greeting(name). The program must print nothing on loading; the function preserves the supplied string name. The companion illustrates the main guard, and separate direct/import fixtures verify its two modes.

Complete Label and FramedLabel. Label(text) stores text and render() returns it. FramedLabel inherits the initializer; its render returns the base render result inside square brackets using super(). Preserve the stored text and independent instances.

Implement Duration(minutes) with a minutes property. Numeric nonnegative values are accepted; negative initialization or assignment raises ValueError before changing stored state. Getter returns the current numeric value. Keep the supplied test helper unchanged.

Complete Session.from_minutes as a class method returning cls("Study", minutes), and Session.valid_minutes as a static method returning minutes >= 0. Preserve the provided initializer and SpecialSession subclass. Factory inputs are nonnegative numeric values; the predicate also checks negative numeric values.
Complete countdown(start), yielding start down to 1 lazily. Nonnegative integer inputs only; zero yields nothing.
Complete Countdown as a single-use iterator over start down to 1. __iter__ returns self; __next__ returns one value and advances, or raises StopIteration. Inputs are nonnegative integers.

Define MinuteError(ValueError) and parse_minutes(text). Invalid integer text raises MinuteError("whole minutes required") from the conversion ValueError. Integers outside 1..60 raise MinuteError("minutes outside 1..60") with no explicit cause; valid text returns its integer.

Complete save_note(path,text,append=False): write UTF-8 exactly, replacement by default or append when True. Use with, return the character count, and propagate I/O errors. Use disposable virtual files only.

Complete parse_minutes(arguments) with argparse: --minutes is integer 1..60, default 10 when omitted, and abbreviated names are disabled. Preserve SystemExit code 2 rejection. Browser input is a supplied string list, not a host process.

Complete run_case(case_class): load a fresh unittest suite, execute it using an in-memory text stream, and return (testsRun,wasSuccessful()). Do not hardcode success. Native file discovery is a separate optional local exercise.

Complete full_groups(amount, size): return amount // size for integer amount and a positive integer size. Negative amounts follow floor-division semantics. No rounding-to-nearest or truncation toward zero.

Complete select_steps(values, start, stop, step): return the list slice values[start:stop:step]. Inputs are a list and integer bounds with nonzero step. Leave the original list unchanged; the returned outer list is new.
